value.title: Mount Fuji climbing routes
value.content: Mount Fuji stands 3,776 metres (12,389 ft) tall, making it the highest mountain in Japan. It has four main climbing routes. Yoshida is the most popular and has the most huts and first-aid stations. Fujinomiya is the shortest but steepest, and starts from the highest trailhead. Subashiri begins below the tree line and joins Yoshida near the summit. Gotemba is the longest and least crowded, with no huts until high on the mountain. The official climbing season runs from early July to early September. Outside the season the huts close, weather on the upper slopes is severe, and mountain rescue coverage is limited.

value.title: LFP and NMC battery chemistries compared
value.content: Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells reach roughly 160 Wh/kg at the pack level, while nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cells reach roughly 250 Wh/kg. LFP uses no cobalt or nickel, which makes it cheaper and less exposed to supply shocks. LFP cycle life is typically 3,000 to 5,000 cycles against 1,000 to 2,000 for NMC, and LFP tolerates repeated charging to 100 percent. LFP has a higher thermal runaway threshold and is considered the safer chemistry. Its weaknesses are cold-weather performance, where usable capacity can drop sharply below freezing, and a flat voltage curve that makes state-of-charge estimation harder. Automakers have moved standard-range trims to LFP while keeping NMC for long-range and performance trims.

value.title: Choosing a Postgres index type
value.content: B-tree is the default index type in Postgres and handles equality and range queries on ordered data. GIN indexes are designed for composite values where a single row contains many keys, such as jsonb documents, arrays, and full-text search vectors; the jsonb_path_ops operator class produces a smaller GIN index that supports containment queries only. GiST supports geometric and nearest-neighbour queries. BRIN stores per-block-range summaries rather than per-row entries, so it is tiny and fast to build, but it only helps when the physical row order correlates with the indexed column, which is typical for append-only time-series tables. Every index adds write amplification on insert and update, and partial indexes with a WHERE clause reduce that cost when queries only touch a subset of rows.

value.title: Evidence on sleep quality and evening routines
value.content: Adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep per night. Sleep proceeds in cycles of roughly 90 minutes alternating between NREM and REM stages, with deep NREM concentrated in the first half of the night and REM in the second. Caffeine has a half-life of about 5 to 6 hours, so an afternoon dose still has meaningful blood levels at bedtime. Evening light exposure, particularly in the blue part of the spectrum, suppresses melatonin release and delays sleep onset. The most consistently supported intervention is a fixed wake time, because it anchors the circadian phase more reliably than a fixed bedtime. Alcohol shortens sleep onset but fragments the second half of the night and suppresses REM.

value.title: Brewing methods and extraction
value.content: Pour-over uses a medium-fine grind and a 1:15 to 1:17 coffee-to-water ratio, producing a clean cup that highlights acidity, and takes about three minutes of active attention. Espresso uses a fine grind and roughly 9 bars of pressure to pull a 25 to 30 second shot, requiring a grinder that holds its setting and regular dialling in. French press uses a coarse grind and a four-minute steep, needs no filter papers, and produces a heavier body because oils and fines pass into the cup. Recommended brew water temperature is 92 to 96 degrees Celsius across methods. Under-extraction tastes sour and thin; over-extraction tastes bitter and drying.

value.title: Research on hybrid work and productivity
value.content: A randomised trial at a large travel agency found hybrid workers matched or slightly exceeded office productivity while attrition fell by about a third. Most published hybrid policies require two to three days per week in the office. Studies consistently find that coordination costs rise when in-office days are not aligned across a team, which is why anchor days outperform per-person choice. The clearest negative finding concerns junior employees: onboarding and skill transfer depend on incidental observation and unplanned feedback, and remote-first onboarding measurably slows time to competence. Fully remote arrangements show the widest variance in outcomes, with results depending heavily on written communication norms.

Write an article titled "How to Care for a Cast Iron Skillet" with H2 headings.

I wrote the article with H2 sections on cleaning, drying, seasoning, and storage.

````draft
title: How to Care for a Cast Iron Skillet

# How to Care for a Cast Iron Skillet

A cast iron skillet can last for generations. It heats evenly, moves from stovetop to oven, and gets better with use. The catch is that it needs a little care that stainless steel pans do not.

## Clean It While It Is Warm

Rinse the skillet with hot water right after cooking and scrub off food with a brush or a chain-mail scrubber. A small drop of mild dish soap is fine on a well-seasoned pan. Avoid soaking it in the sink, which invites rust.

## Dry It Completely

Water is the main enemy of cast iron. Towel the skillet dry, then set it over low heat for a minute or two until every trace of moisture is gone.

## Season It Regularly

Seasoning is a thin layer of polymerized oil that protects the iron and keeps food from sticking. Rub a very thin coat of neutral oil over the warm pan, wipe off the excess, and heat it until it just starts to smoke. Repeat whenever the surface looks dull or dry.

## Store It Dry

Keep the skillet in a dry cupboard. If you stack pans, put a paper towel inside to absorb moisture and protect the surface.

## Fixing Rust

If rust appears, scrub it off with steel wool, wash and dry the pan, and season it two or three times. The skillet will be as good as new.
````

value.name: Validate tag and choose branch
value.run:
set -euo pipefail
TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

# Validate semver-like tag: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE]
if [[ ! "$TAG" =~ ^v([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+)(-.+)?$ ]]; then
  echo "::error::Invalid semver tag: $TAG"; exit 1
fi

MAJOR="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
MINOR="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
PATCH="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
PRERE="${BASH_REMATCH[4]:-}"
BASE="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"

if [[ -n "$PRERE" ]]; then
  echo "prerelease=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  # Candidate release branches for pre-releases (highest priority first)
  CANDIDATES=(
    "origin/${BASE}"
    "origin/release/${BASE}"
    "origin/v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}"
    "origin/release/v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}"
  )
else
  echo "prerelease=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  CANDIDATES=("origin/main")
fi

git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*

TARGET=""
for ref in "${CANDIDATES[@]}"; do
  if git rev-parse --verify -q "$ref" >/dev/null; then
    if git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" "$ref"; then
      TARGET="$ref"; break
    fi
  fi
done

if [[ -z "$TARGET" ]]; then
  echo "allowed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::warning::Tag $TAG is not contained in any target branch candidate (${CANDIDATES[*]}). Skipping release."
else
  echo "allowed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "targetBranch=$TARGET" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "Selected target: $TARGET"
fi

# Secrets are absent on a fork and on any repo that has not
# configured them. Failing there would put a red mark on every PR
# touching evals for a reason the author cannot fix.
if [ -z "$LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY" ] || [ -z "$LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY" ] || [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
  echo "::warning::Eval skipped: OPENAI_API_KEY / LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY / LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY are not all configured for this repository."

fi
# A dispatch may ask for one mode. The matrix still expands to both,
# so the other leg reports itself as skipped rather than measuring
# something nobody asked for.
if [ -n "$SELECTED_MODE" ] && [ "$SELECTED_MODE" != both ] && [ "$SELECTED_MODE" != "$MODE" ]; then
  echo "::notice::Eval skipped: this dispatch selected mode '$SELECTED_MODE'."

fi

file_enhancements.explanation: Configures the SearXNG rate limiter and bot detection. The summary shows no parsed settings, so the file may be empty or comment-only.
file_enhancements.best_practice: If the file is empty, either define explicit limiter rules or remove it and document that the defaults are intended.
file_enhancements.security_concern: Verify that rate limiting is active if the SearXNG instance can be reached from outside the Docker network; an empty file provides no custom protection.
file_enhancements.context: Abuse protection for the self-hosted search backend

file_enhancements.explanation: Defines the morphic-stack services, including the Morphic app, which runs next start bound to 0.0.0.0. Its image defaults to a placeholder GitHub repository when GITHUB_REPOSITORY is unset.
file_enhancements.best_practice: Require GITHUB_REPOSITORY using ${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?error} or default to the official image, and pin images to a version tag or digest.
file_enhancements.security_concern: The your-username/morphic fallback could pull an image from an unintended GHCR namespace if the variable is unset. Also verify that published ports are limited to services that need external access.
file_enhancements.migration_suggestion: Keep shared environment values in an env_file instead of repeating them across services, if the full file shows duplication.

file_enhancements.explanation: Template for local environment variables, including the OpenAI key, database URL and Tavily key. The values shown are placeholders.
file_enhancements.best_practice: Mark each variable as required or optional, and validate the environment at application startup with a schema.
file_enhancements.migration_suggestion: Use this file as the single reference for environment variables and keep it in sync with docker-compose.yaml.

file_enhancements.explanation: Builds the Morphic container image and sets MORPHIC_INSTALL_METHOD to docker. It also includes a localhost DATABASE_URL with placeholder credentials, probably to satisfy build-time checks.
file_enhancements.best_practice: Scope the placeholder DATABASE_URL to the build step, for example with an inline variable on RUN, so it doesn't remain in the final image.
file_enhancements.security_concern: Placeholder credentials are hardcoded (user:pass). They don't appear to be real secrets, but if they persist in the runtime image, a misconfigured deployment could use them silently instead of failing fast.

file_enhancements.explanation: Registers the next-devtools MCP server for MCP-compatible tools, launched over stdio through npx.
file_enhancements.best_practice: Pin next-devtools-mcp to a specific version and update it deliberately.
file_enhancements.security_concern: Running next-devtools-mcp@latest through npx executes whatever version is newest on each fresh resolve, which exposes developer machines to supply-chain risk.

file_enhancements.explanation: Defines the project's Prettier formatting rules. The summary shows no parsed settings because the JavaScript config wasn't statically extracted.

file_enhancements.explanation: Defines the private morphic package at version 1.10.0, along with its scripts, dependencies and related metadata (119 settings in total).
file_enhancements.best_practice: Commit a lockfile, use frozen installs in CI, and pin the package manager and Node version with packageManager and engines if they aren't already set.

file_enhancements.explanation: Configures SearXNG on top of its default settings, with the server listening on 0.0.0.0:8888.
